observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a ceramic plate with a dark outer rim and pale interior, resting on a dark wooden surface under cool bluish light. In the center of the plate sits a small conical mound of white granular material, surrounded by a shallow, irregular pool of clear liquid. A thin plant-stem shadow/reflection runs vertically across the liquid below the mound. The plate, mound, liquid pool, and stem shadow all remain in fixed positions throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The white mound stays centered and roughly the same size and height from first to last frame; no translation or expansion is seen.
A small bright bubble / wet highlight becomes visible at the lower edge of the mound in the middle-to-late frames, where it is absent or barely visible at the start.
The granular texture on the mound's surface appears marginally smoother and wetter toward the end of the segment, a subtle change consistent with slow interaction with the surrounding liquid.
The outline of the liquid pool and the position of the stem shadow/reflection do not move, indicating no spreading or flow.
Only slight frame-to-frame brightness/exposure flicker is observed; there is no evident camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the mound had already begun dissolving before this segment or continues to dissolve after it.
The actual identity of the granular material and the liquid.
The cause of the small bubble appearing at the mound's base.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent softening of the mound's surface is a real physical change or partly an artifact of exposure flicker.
Whether any very small camera jitter is present, given the static background.
The exact timing of the bubble's first appearance due to subtle contrast changes between frames.
